answer: Make trust grow slowly: a new agent starts on a small knoll of privileges and must complete many small, time-staked jobs before it earns full economic rights. At the kernel of the design is a vesting bond — each completed job locks a sliver of earnings for weeks, so one operator running many fake identities must fund and babysit every identity for months while earning almost nothing. Like onyx forming slowly under pressure, reputation that takes real calendar time to build cannot be faked at scale, and any identity caught sharing an operator with another forfeits its whole vested bond.
